question: In a circle centered at O, a diameter AB is extended to a point C outside the circle. CD is a tangent at point D on the circle. If CD = 7√3 cm and ∠DBC = 120°, then the length of the diameter of the circle is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since ABC forms a straight line, ∠OBD = 180° − 120° = 60°.

Because OB and OD are radii, ΔOBD is equilateral, making ∠BOD = 60°.

The tangent CD is perpendicular to radius OD, so ∠ODC = 90°.

In right-angled ΔODC, tan(60°) = CD ÷ OD ⇒ √3 = 7√3 ÷ R.

Solving this gives R = 7 cm. The diameter is 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.**
